who: T. Walter (Thomas Walter) Wallbank, world historian at the University of Southern California, 1933–1964.

evidence.says: The authority's citation for Civilization past & present identifies T. Walter Wallbank as emeritus professor of history at the University of Southern California.
Identifies Thomas Walter Wallbank as the textbook author and states that he taught history at USC from 1933 to 1964.

notes: The candidate's institution and teaching period agree with the USC dissertations of 1954–1959.

who: A. Michal McMahon, historian at West Virginia University, PhD University of Texas.

evidence.says: The history faculty list includes emeritus faculty member A. Michal McMahon, PhD University of Texas.
The catalogue credits A. Michal (Adrian Michal) McMahon as editor of the Franklin Institute Committee on Science and the Arts records.
This Michael McMahon is a secondary-school teacher and author of The murder of Thomas Douglas Bateson, County Monaghan, 1851.
This Michael Francis McMahon is a macroeconomist at the University of Oxford, associated with work on investment and monetary policy.
The Michael B. McMahon authority supplies a citation to Páramos en la memoria, without an institutional or degree connection to WVU.
The authority cites Michael McMahon's Metro's housing company, without establishing a connection to the WVU historian.

notes: Reviewed all 19 supplied LC authorities; none establishes the WVU/Texas identity. Several describe clearly different careers, but sparse records prevent confidently rejecting the entire set. The supervisor's documented name is A. Michal, expanded in the catalogue as Adrian Michal, rather than Michael.

who: Noel Emmanuel Lenski, Yale professor of classics and history, PhD Princeton 1995, specializing in Roman history and Late Antiquity.

Princeton identifies Noel Emmanuel Lenski as a 1995 Classics PhD, with the dissertation Valens and the Forth Century Empire.
The authority connects Noel Emmanuel Lenski with the 1995 dissertation Valens and the fourth century empire and Noel Lenski's Failure of empire.

notes: The full name, dissertation, Princeton doctorate and Yale appointment agree with the supervisor's degree and students' institution and period.

who: Alexander A. Vasiliev, historian of Byzantium and history professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in the 1930s.

evidence.says: The department lists Alexander Vasiliev as advisor to Peter Charanis in 1934–1935, Kostis Argoe in 1937–1938, Hazel Ramsay in 1932–1933 and John Schneider in 1930–1931.
The Wisconsin Historical Society identifies its 1934 portrait as University of Wisconsin history professor Alexander A. Vasiliev.
The candidate is Alexander N. Vasiliev, author of Low-dimensional magnetism and head of the Solid State Physics Division and Low Temperature Physics Department at Moscow State University.

notes: The sole supplied candidate is a physicist with a different middle initial, not the Wisconsin historian. The university's records directly identify several listed students and their advisor.

who: Stuart Alan Kirsch, University of Michigan anthropologist affiliated with Anthropology and History, PhD Pennsylvania 1991.

evidence.says: Michigan identifies Kirsch as professor of anthropology, PhD Pennsylvania, affiliated with Anthropology and History, and author of Reverse Anthropology and Engaged Anthropology.
The appointment document states that Kirsch earned his Pennsylvania doctorate in 1991, joined Michigan in 1995 and became professor in 2014.
The authority identifies the author as Michigan anthropology professor Stuart Kirsch, PhD Pennsylvania 1991; an author correction establishes Alan as his middle name.

notes: Institution, degree and publications agree. His Anthropology and History affiliation accounts for his appearance among history dissertation supervisors.

who: Timothy J. A. Le Goff, historian of eighteenth-century France at York University, PhD London.

evidence.says: York's faculty list identifies Timothy J. Le Goff, PhD London, as associate professor of history.
The indexed archival description identifies T. J. A. Le Goff as a York history faculty member from 1969 and author of Vannes and its region, concerning eighteenth-century France.
Thomas N. Goff is a research chemist at the Albany Metallurgy Research Center, associated with phosphate-processing publications.
Thomas George Goff is the author of Theory and practice of investment.
The Tim Goff authority cites Under both flags, 2003, with Tim Groff noted as the title-page spelling, but supplies no university or degree identification.

notes: The two Thomas Goff authorities are different people. The sparse Tim Goff record cannot be securely identified or excluded; no supplied authority establishes the York historian's identity. York archival information was available through its indexed description; direct access required browser verification.

who: Raymond Francis Bulman, professor of theology and philosophy of religion at St. John's University, Queens, from 1963.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Raymond F. Bulman as Raymond Francis Bulman, author of A blueprint for humanity and From Trent to Vatican II, and professor at St. John's University since 1963.
The society bulletin's indexed obituary identifies Raymond Francis Bulman as professor of systematic theology and philosophy of religion at St. John's University in Jamaica, Queens, since 1963.
The alternative Ray Bulman authority identifies a powerboat racer, journalist and author of British offshore powerboat marathons.

notes: Raymond F. Bulman's institution and career period agree with the St. John's dissertations of 2002–2013. The alternative Ray Bulman is a different person.
